thread.title: Close Update: S&P, Nasdaq Slide for Third Day as Energy, Tech Stocks Weigh

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: S&P, Nasdaq Slide for Third Day as Energy, Tech Stocks Weigh
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street was dented on Thursday by losses in energy and information technology that weighed on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, sending the measures down for a third straight session, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average bucked the trend and ended with slim gains for a second day.
A downbeat day for chip stocks and a retreat in oil prices outweighed rises in the S&P's telecoms and utilities groups. The consumer components were split, with staples gaining about 0.2% late in the session and discretionary down by about 0.3%.
Tech shares have come under sharp selling pressure this week after social-media company leaders testified to lawmakers in Washington, D.C. Facebook ( FB ) fell for a second day, sliding 2.8% while Amazon.com ( AMZN ) slipped 1.8% and Apple ( AAPL ) shed 1.7%.
And on Thursday, semiconductor company KLA-Tencor ( KLAC ) added to the sector's woes, with its CFO warning of slowing memory chip growth, Reuters said. The stock sank 9.7% by the bell. Downbeat views sent Micron Technology ( MU ) down 9.9% after Baird lowered its price target on the stock to $75 from $100. Applied Materials (AMAT) shed 5.3% and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) lost 2.4%.
The S&P's tech group ended 0.8% lower. But the steepest loss came in energy, which shed 1.9% as oil prices tumbled after weekly crude stockpiles data showed a bigger-than-expected increase in gasoline inventories, raising concerns about demand. Chevron (CVX) had the largest slide on the Dow, skidding 3.1% and Exxon Mobil (XOM) decreased 1.1%.
The day's economic data was heavy, with job-market indicators showing a smaller-than-expected ADP private payrolls gain but a slide in weekly jobless claims to the lowest in almost 49 years. That's ahead of Friday's closely watched non-farm payrolls report, which is expected to show additions of 195,000 jobs and a slight decrease in the unemployment rate to 3.8%, according to Econoday.
